Main.sentence: Jesus [e] ( c. 6 to 4 BC – AD 30 or 33), also referred to as Jesus Christ , [f] Jesus of Nazareth , and many ___E:other names and titles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Names_and_titles_of_Jesus_in_the_New_Testament)___ , was a 1st-century ___E:Jewish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish)___ preacher and religious leader in the ___E:Roman province of Judaea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_province_of_Judaea)___ .

He is the ___E:central figure U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_in_Christianity)___ of ___E:Christianity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity)___ , the ___E:world's largest religion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_religious_groups)___ .

Most ___E:Christians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christians)___ consider Jesus to be the ___E:incarnation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incarnation_(Christianity))___ of ___E:God the Son U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_the_Son)___ and awaited ___E:messiah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messiah#Christianity)___ , or ___E:Christ U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christ_(title))___ , a descendant from the ___E:Davidic line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davidic_line)___ that is prophesied in the ___E:Old Testament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Testament)___ .

Virtually all modern scholars of ___E:antiquity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_antiquity)___ agree that ___E:Jesus existed historically U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historicity_of_Jesus)___ . [g] Accounts of ___E:Jesus's life U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_of_Jesus)___ are contained in the ___E:Gospels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel)___ , especially the ___E:four canonical Gospels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_canonical_Gospels)___ in the ___E:New Testament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Testament)___ .

Since the ___E:Enlightenment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age_of_Enlightenment)___ , ___E:academic research U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quest_for_the_historical_Jesus)___ has yielded various views on the ___E:historical reliability of the Gospels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_reliability_of_the_Gospels)___ and how closely they reflect the ___E:historical Jesus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_Jesus)___ .  [h]

According to Christian tradition, as preserved in the Gospels and the ___E:Acts of the Apostles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acts_of_the_Apostles)___ , Jesus ___E:was circumcised U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circumcision_of_Jesus)___ at eight days old, ___E:was baptized U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptism_of_Jesus)___ by ___E:John the Baptist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_the_Baptist)___ as a young adult, and after 40 days and nights of fasting in the wilderness, began ___E:his own ministry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Jesus)___ .

He was an ___E:itinerant teacher U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itinerant_teacher)___ who interpreted the ___E:law of God U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biblical_law)___ with divine authority and was often referred to as " ___E:rabbi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbi)___ ".

Jesus often debated with his fellow Jews on how to best follow ___E:God U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_in_Christianity)___ , engaged in healings, taught in ___E:parables U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parables_of_Jesus)___ , and gathered followers, among whom 12 were appointed as his ___E:apostles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostles_in_the_New_Testament)___ .

He was arrested in ___E:Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem)___ and tried by the ___E:Jewish authorities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanhedrin)___ ,  handed over to the ___E:Roman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome)___ government, and ___E:crucified U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucifixion_of_Jesus)___ on the order of ___E:Pontius Pilate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontius_Pilate)___ , the ___E:Roman prefect U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_governor)___ of ___E:Judaea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaea_(Roman_province))___ .

After his death, his followers became convinced that he ___E:rose from the dead U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resurrection_of_Jesus)___ , and following his ascension, the community they formed eventually became the ___E:early Christian Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Christian_Church)___ that expanded as a ___E:worldwide movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spread_of_Christianity)___ .

___E:Christian theology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_theology)___ includes the beliefs that Jesus was conceived by the ___E:Holy Spirit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Spirit_in_Christianity)___ , was ___E:born of a virgin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_birth_of_Jesus)___ named ___E:Mary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary,_mother_of_Jesus)___ , performed ___E:miracles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miracles_of_Jesus)___ , founded the ___E:Christian Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Church)___ , ___E:died by crucifixion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucifixion_of_Jesus)___ as a sacrifice to achieve ___E:atonement for sin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atonement_in_Christianity)___ , rose from the dead, and ___E:ascended U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascension_of_Jesus)___ into ___E:Heaven U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heaven_in_Christianity)___ from where he ___E:will return U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Coming)___ .

Commonly, Christians believe Jesus enables people to be reconciled to God. The ___E:Nicene Creed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicene_Creed)___ asserts that Jesus will ___E:judge the living and the dead U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Judgment)___ , either ___E:before U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intermediate_state_(Christianity))___ or ___E:after U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_mortalism)___ their ___E:bodily resurrection U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resurrection_of_the_dead#Christianity)___ , an event tied to the Second Coming of Jesus in ___E:Christian eschatology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_eschatology)___ .

The great majority of Christians worship Jesus as the incarnation of God the Son, the second of three ___E:persons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prosopon)___ of the ___E:Trinity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity)___ . [i] The ___E:birth of Jesus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_of_Jesus)___ is celebrated annually, generally on 25 December, [j] as ___E:Christmas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas)___ .
His crucifixion is honoured on ___E:Good Friday U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Friday)___ and his resurrection on ___E:Easter Sunday U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Sunday)___ .

The world's most widely used ___E:calendar era U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calendar_era)___ —in which the current year is AD 2025 (or 2025 ___E:CE U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Era)___ )—was based on the approximate ___E:date of the birth of Jesus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Date_of_the_birth_of_Jesus)___ .

___E:Judaism rejects the belief U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_views_on_Jesus)___ that Jesus was the awaited messiah, arguing that he did not fulfill ___E:messianic prophecies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messiah_in_Judaism)___ , was not ___E:lawfully anointed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anointing)___ and was neither divine nor resurrected.

In contrast, ___E:Jesus in Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_in_Islam)___ [k] is considered the ___E:messiah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messiah#Islam)___ and a ___E:prophet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prophets_and_messengers_in_Islam)___ of ___E:God U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_in_Islam)___ , who was sent to the ___E:Israelites U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israelites)___ and ___E:will return to Earth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Coming#Islam)___ before the ___E:Day of Judgement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judgement_Day_in_Islam)___ . ___E:Muslims U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims)___ believe Jesus was born of the virgin ___E:Mary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_in_Islam)___ but was neither God nor a son of God. Most Muslims ___E:do not believe that he was killed or crucified U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_views_on_Jesus%27s_death)___ but that God ___E:raised him into Heaven while he was still alive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entering_heaven_alive)___ . [l] Jesus is also revered in the ___E:Baháʼí U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD_Faith)___ and the ___E:Druze faiths U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Druze_faith)___ , as well as in the ___E:Rastafari U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rastafari)___ .

A typical Jew in Jesus's time ___E:had only one name U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_name)___ , sometimes followed by a ___E:patronymic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patronymic)___ phrase of the form "son of [father's name]", or the person's home town.  Thus, in the New Testament, Jesus is commonly referred to as "Jesus of ___E:Nazareth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazareth)___ ". [m] Jesus's neighbours in Nazareth referred to him as "the carpenter, the son of ___E:Mary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary,_mother_of_Jesus)___ and brother of ___E:James U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James,_brother_of_Jesus)___ and ___E:Joses U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joses,_brother_of_James_the_younger)___ and ___E:Judas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jude,_brother_of_Jesus)___ and ___E:Simon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon,_brother_of_Jesus)___ ", "the carpenter's son", or " ___E:Joseph U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Joseph)___ 's son"; in the Gospel of John, the disciple ___E:Philip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_the_Apostle)___ refers to him as "Jesus son of Joseph from Nazareth".

The English name Jesus ( ___E:Ancient Greek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language)___ : Ἰησοῦς , romanized Iēsous ) is a rendering of Joshua ( ___E:Hebrew U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew)___ or ___E:Aramaic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aramaic)___ : יֵשׁוּעַ , romanized Yehoshua , later Yeshua ), and was not uncommon in Judea at the time of the birth of Jesus.

The ___E:Gospel of Matthew U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_Matthew)___ tells of an ___E:angel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel)___ that appeared to Joseph instructing him "to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins".
Since the early period [timeframe?] of Christianity, Christians have commonly referred to Jesus as "Jesus Christ".

The word Christ was a ___E:title or office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threefold_office)___ ("the Christ"), not a given name.   It derives from the Greek Χριστός ( Christos ),   a translation of the Hebrew mashiakh ( משיח ) meaning ' ___E:anointed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anointed)___ ', and is usually transliterated into English as messiah .
In biblical Judaism, ___E:sacred oil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_anointing_oil)___ was used to anoint certain exceptionally holy people and objects as part of their religious investiture.

Christians of the time designated Jesus as "the Christ" because they believed him to be the messiah, whose arrival is ___E:prophesied U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_and_messianic_prophecy)___ in the ___E:Hebrew Bible U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_Bible)___ and Old Testament.
In postbiblical usage, Christ became viewed as a name—one part of "Jesus Christ".
The term Christian (meaning a follower of Christ) has been in use since the 1st century.

The four ___E:canonical gospels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canonical_gospel)___ ( ___E:Matthew U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_Matthew)___ , ___E:Mark U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_Mark)___ , ___E:Luke U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_Luke)___ , and ___E:John U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_John)___ ) are the foremost sources for the life and message of Jesus.

But other parts of the New Testament also include references to key episodes in his life, such as the ___E:Last Supper U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Supper)___ in ___E:1 Corinthians 11 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1_Corinthians_11)___ :23–26.     ___E:Acts of the Apostles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acts_of_the_Apostles)___  refers to Jesus's early ministry and its anticipation by ___E:John the Baptist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_the_Baptist)___ .

Acts 1:1–11  says more about the ___E:Ascension of Jesus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascension_of_Jesus)___  than the canonical gospels do.  In the ___E:undisputed Pauline letters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauline_epistles#Authenticity)___ , which were written earlier than the Gospels, Jesus's words or instructions are cited several times.  [n]
Some ___E:early Christian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Christian)___ groups had separate descriptions of Jesus's life and teachings that are not in the New Testament.

These include the ___E:Gospel of Thomas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_Thomas)___ , ___E:Gospel of Peter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_Peter)___ , and ___E:Gospel of Judas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_Judas)___ , the ___E:Apocryphon of James U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apocryphon_of_James)___ , and ___E:many other apocryphal writings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Testament_apocrypha)___ .
Most scholars conclude that these were written much later and are less reliable accounts than the canonical gospels.
The canonical gospels are four accounts, each by a different author.

The authors of the Gospels are pseudonymous, attributed by tradition to the ___E:four evangelists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_evangelists)___ , each with close ties to Jesus:  Mark by ___E:John Mark U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mark)___ , an associate of ___E:Peter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter)___ ;  ___E:Matthew U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_the_Apostle)___ by one of Jesus's disciples;  ___E:Luke U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_the_Evangelist)___ by a companion of ___E:Paul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_the_Apostle)___ mentioned in a few epistles;  and John by another of Jesus's disciples,  the " ___E:beloved disciple U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beloved_disciple)___ ".

According to the ___E:Marcan priority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcan_priority)___ , the first to be written was the Gospel of Mark (written AD 60–75), followed by the Gospel of Matthew (AD 65–85), the Gospel of Luke (AD 65–95), and the Gospel of John (AD 75–100).
Most scholars agree that the authors of Matthew and Luke used Mark as a source for their gospels.

Since Matthew and Luke also share some content not found in Mark, many scholars assume that they used another source (commonly called the " ___E:Q source U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Q_source)___ ") in addition to Mark.

One important aspect of the study of the Gospels is the ___E:literary genre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literary_genre)___ under which they fall. Genre "is a key convention guiding both the composition and the interpretation of writings".
Whether the gospel authors set out to write novels, myths, histories, or biographies has a tremendous impact on how they ought to be interpreted.
Some studies have suggested that the Gospels ought to be seen as ancient biography.
Although not without critics,  the position that the Gospels are a type of ancient biography is the consensus among scholars today.

Concerning the accuracy of the accounts, viewpoints range from considering them ___E:inerrant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inerrant)___ descriptions of Jesus's life,  to doubting whether they are historically reliable on various points,  to considering them to provide very little historical information about his life beyond the basics.

According to a broad scholarly consensus, the ___E:Synoptic Gospels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synoptic_Gospels)___ (the first three—Matthew, Mark, and Luke) are the most reliable sources of information about Jesus.

Matthew, Mark, and Luke are known as the Synoptic Gospels, from the Greek σύν ( syn , 'together') and ὄψις ( opsis , 'view'),    because they are similar in content, narrative arrangement, language and paragraph structure, and one can easily set them next to each other and synoptically compare what is in them.    Scholars generally agree that it is impossible to find any direct literary relationship between the Synoptic Gospels and the Gospel of John.  Many events (e.g., Jesus's baptism, ___E:transfiguration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfiguration_of_Jesus)___ , crucifixion and interactions with his ___E:apostles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostles_in_the_New_Testament)___ ) appear in the Synoptic Gospels, but incidents such as the transfiguration and Jesus's exorcising demons  do not appear in John, which also differs on other matters, such as the ___E:cleansing of the Temple U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleansing_of_the_Temple)___ .
The Synoptics emphasize different aspects of Jesus.

In Mark, Jesus is the ___E:Son of God U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_of_God_(Christianity))___ whose mighty works demonstrate the presence of ___E:God's Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God%27s_Kingdom)___ .
He is a tireless wonder worker, the servant of both God and man.  This short gospel records a few of Jesus's words or teachings.
The Gospel of Matthew emphasizes that Jesus is the fulfilment of God's will as revealed in the Old Testament, and the Lord of the Church.
He is the " ___E:Son of David U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davidic_line)___ ", a "king", and the Messiah.
Luke presents Jesus as the divine-human saviour who shows compassion to the needy.

He is the friend of sinners and outcasts, and came to seek and save the lost.  This gospel includes well-known parables, such as the ___E:Good Samaritan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Samaritan)___ and the ___E:Prodigal Son U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prodigal_Son)___ .

The ___E:prologue to the Gospel of John U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prologue_to_the_Gospel_of_John)___ identifies Jesus as an incarnation of the divine Word ( ___E:Logos U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logos_(Christianity))___ ).
As the Word, Jesus was eternally present with God, active in all creation, and the source of humanity's moral and spiritual nature.

Jesus is not only greater than any past human prophet but greater than any prophet could be. He not only speaks God's Word; he is God's Word.  In the Gospel of John, Jesus reveals his divine role publicly.

Here he is the ___E:Bread of Life U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bread_of_Life)___ , the ___E:Light of the World U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_of_the_World)___ , the ___E:True Vine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_Vine)___ , and more.

The authors of the New Testament generally showed little interest in an absolute ___E:chronology of Jesus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chronology_of_Jesus)___ or in synchronizing the episodes of his life with the secular history of the age.  As stated in ___E:John 21:25 U:(https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Bible_(American_Standard)/John#21:25)___ , the Gospels do not claim to provide an exhaustive list of the events of Jesus's life.  The accounts were primarily written as theological documents in the context of ___E:early Christianity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Christianity)___ , with timelines as a secondary consideration.

The Gospels devote about one third of their text to the last week of Jesus's life in ___E:Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem)___ , referred to as ___E:the Passion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passion_(Christianity))___ .
They do not provide enough details to satisfy the demands of modern historians regarding exact dates, but it is possible to draw from them a general picture of Jesus's life story.
Jesus was Jewish,  born to Mary, wife of ___E:Joseph U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Joseph)___ .
The Gospels of Matthew and Luke offer two accounts of his ___E:genealogy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genealogy)___ .
Matthew traces Jesus's ancestry to ___E:Abraham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham)___ through ___E:David U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David)___ .
Luke traces Jesus's ancestry through ___E:Adam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam)___ to God.   The lists are identical between Abraham and David but differ radically from that point.

Matthew has 27 generations from David to Joseph, whereas Luke has 42, with almost no overlap between the names on the two lists. [o]  Various theories have been put forward to explain why the two genealogies are so different. [p]

Both Matthew and Luke describe Jesus's birth, especially that Jesus was born to a virgin named Mary in ___E:Bethlehem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethlehem)___ in fulfilment of ___E:prophecy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prophecy)___ .

Luke's account emphasizes events before the ___E:birth of Jesus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_of_Jesus)___ and centres on Mary, while Matthew's mostly covers those after the birth and centres on Joseph.

Both accounts state that Mary was engaged to a man named Joseph, who was descended from King David and was not his biological father, and both support the doctrine of the ___E:virgin birth of Jesus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_birth_of_Jesus)___ , according to which Jesus was miraculously conceived by the ___E:Holy Spirit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Spirit)___ in Mary's womb when she was still a virgin.

At the same time, there is evidence, at least in the Lukan Acts of the Apostles, that Jesus was thought to have had, like many figures in antiquity, a dual paternity, since there it is stated he descended from the seed or loins of David.
By ___E:taking him as his own U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adoption_in_Judaism)___ , Joseph will give him the necessary Davidic descent.

Some scholars suggest that Jesus had ___E:Levite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levite)___ heritage from Mary, based on her blood relationship with ___E:Elizabeth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_(biblical_figure))___ .

In Matthew, Joseph is troubled because Mary, his betrothed, is pregnant,  but in the first of ___E:Joseph's four dreams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph%27s_dream)___ an angel assures him not to be afraid to take Mary as his wife because her child was conceived by the Holy Spirit.

In ___E:Matthew 2:1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_2:1)___ – ___E:12 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_2:12)___ , ___E:wise men U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biblical_Magi)___ or ___E:Magi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magi)___ from the East bring gifts to the young Jesus as the ___E:King of the Jews U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus,_King_of_the_Jews)___ .

They find him in a house in Bethlehem. ___E:Herod the Great U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herod_the_Great)___ hears of Jesus's birth and, wanting him killed, ___E:orders the murders of male infants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massacre_of_the_Innocents)___ in Bethlehem and its surroundings.
However, an angel warns Joseph in his second dream, and the family ___E:flees to Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_to_Egypt)___ —later to return and settle in Nazareth.
In Luke 1:31–38, Mary learns from the angel ___E:Gabriel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel)___ that she will conceive and bear a child called Jesus through the action of the Holy Spirit.

When Mary is due to give birth, she and Joseph travel from Nazareth to Joseph's ancestral home in Bethlehem to register in the census ordered by ___E:Caesar Augustus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesar_Augustus)___ .
While there Mary gives birth to Jesus, and as they have found no room in the inn, she places the newborn in a ___E:manger U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manger)___ .

An ___E:angel announces the birth to a group of shepherds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annunciation_to_the_shepherds)___ , who go to Bethlehem to see Jesus, and subsequently spread the news abroad.

Luke 2:21 tells how Joseph and Mary ___E:have their baby circumcised on the eighth day after birth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circumcision_of_Jesus)___ , and name him Jesus, as Gabriel had commanded Mary.  After the ___E:presentation of Jesus at the Temple U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_of_Jesus_at_the_Temple)___ , Joseph, Mary and Jesus return to Nazareth.

Jesus's childhood home is identified in the Gospels of Luke and Matthew as Nazareth, a town in ___E:Galilee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galilee)___ in present-day ___E:Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)___ , where he lived with his family.
Although Joseph appears in descriptions of Jesus's childhood, no mention is made of him thereafter.

His other family members, including his mother, Mary, ___E:his four brothers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brothers_of_Jesus)___ ___E:James U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James,_brother_of_Jesus)___ , ___E:Joses (or Joseph) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joses,_brother_of_Jesus)___ , ___E:Judas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jude,_brother_of_Jesus)___ , and ___E:Simon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon,_brother_of_Jesus)___ , and his unnamed sisters, are mentioned in the Gospels and other sources.

Jesus's maternal grandparents are named ___E:Joachim U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joachim)___ and ___E:Anne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Anne)___ in the ___E:Gospel of James U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_of_James)___ .
The Gospel of Luke records that Mary was a relative of Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist.

Extra-biblical contemporary sources consider Jesus and John the Baptist to be second cousins through the belief that Elizabeth was the daughter of ___E:Sobe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobe_(sister_of_Saint_Anne))___ , the sister of Anne.
The Gospel of Mark reports that at the beginning of ___E:his ministry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Jesus)___ , Jesus comes into conflict with his neighbours and family.
Jesus's mother and brothers come to get him  because people are saying that ___E:he is mentally ill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_health_of_Jesus)___ .
Jesus responds that his followers are his true family.
In the Gospel of John, Jesus and his mother attend a ___E:wedding at Cana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wedding_at_Cana)___ , where he performs his first miracle at her request.
Later, she follows him to his crucifixion, and he expresses concern over her well-being.

Jesus is called a τέκτων ( tektōn ) in ___E:Mark 6:3 U:(https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Bible_(American_Standard)/Mark#6:3)___ , a term traditionally understood as carpenter but which could also refer to makers of objects in various materials, including builders.
Given the term's broad semantic range and "the socio-historical reality of a common Nazarene τέκτων", Matthew K. Robinson, minister and academic, prefers to translate τέκτων as 'builder-craftsman'.
The Gospels indicate that Jesus could read, paraphrase, and debate scripture, but this does not necessarily mean that he received formal scribal training.
The Gospel of Luke reports two journeys of Jesus and his parents in Jerusalem during his childhood.

They come to the ___E:Temple in Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_in_Jerusalem)___ for the ___E:presentation of Jesus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presentation_of_Jesus)___ as a baby in accordance with Jewish Law, where a man named ___E:Simeon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simeon_(Gospel_of_Luke))___ prophesies about Jesus and Mary.  When Jesus, at the age of twelve, goes missing on a pilgrimage to Jerusalem for ___E:Passover U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passover)___ , his parents ___E:find him in the temple U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finding_in_the_Temple)___ sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking questions, and the people are amazed at his understanding and answers.
Mary scolds Jesus for going missing, to which Jesus replies that he must "be in his father's house".

The ___E:synoptic gospels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synoptic_gospels)___ describe ___E:Jesus's baptism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptism_of_Jesus)___ in the ___E:Jordan River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_River)___ and ___E:the temptations he suffered U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temptation_of_Christ)___ while spending forty days in the ___E:Judaean Desert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaean_Desert)___ , as a preparation for his public ministry.
The accounts of Jesus's baptism are all preceded by information about John the Baptist.

They show John preaching penance and repentance for the remission of sins and encouraging the giving of ___E:alms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alms)___ to the poor  as he baptizes people in the area of the Jordan River around ___E:Perea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perea)___ and foretells the arrival of someone "more powerful" than he.

In the Gospel of Mark, John the Baptist baptizes Jesus, and as he comes out of the water he sees the ___E:Holy Spirit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Spirit)___ descending to him like a dove and a voice comes from heaven declaring him to be God's Son.  This is one of two events described in the Gospels where a voice from Heaven calls Jesus "Son", the other being the ___E:Transfiguration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfiguration_of_Jesus)___ .
The spirit then drives him into the wilderness where he is tempted by ___E:Satan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satan)___ .
Jesus then begins his ministry in Galilee after John's arrest.
In the Gospel of Matthew, as Jesus comes to him to be baptized, John protests, saying, "I need to be baptized by you."  Jesus instructs him to carry on with the baptism "to fulfil all righteousness".
Matthew details three temptations that Satan offers Jesus in the wilderness.
In the Gospel of Luke, the Holy Spirit descends as a dove after everyone has been baptized and Jesus is ___E:praying U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prayers_of_Jesus)___ .

Later John implicitly recognizes Jesus after sending his followers to ask about him.  Luke also describes three temptations received by Jesus in the wilderness, before starting his ministry in Galilee.
The Gospel of John leaves out Jesus's baptism and temptation.
Here, John the Baptist testifies that he saw the Spirit descend on Jesus.
John publicly proclaims Jesus as the sacrificial ___E:Lamb of God U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamb_of_God)___ , and some of John's followers become disciples of Jesus.
Before John is imprisoned, Jesus leads his followers to baptize disciples as well,  and they baptize more people than John.
The Synoptics depict two distinct geographical settings in Jesus's ministry.

The first takes place north of ___E:Judea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judea)___ , in Galilee, where Jesus conducts a successful ministry, and the second shows Jesus rejected and killed when he travels to Jerusalem.
Often referred to as " ___E:rabbi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbi)___ ",  Jesus preaches his message orally.

Jesus forbids those who recognize him as the messiah to speak of it, including people he heals and demons he exorcises (see ___E:Messianic Secret U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messianic_Secret)___ ).
John depicts Jesus's ministry as largely taking place in and around Jerusalem, rather than in Galilee, and Jesus's divine identity is openly proclaimed and immediately recognized.
Scholars divide the ministry of Jesus into several stages.

The Galilean ministry begins when Jesus returns to Galilee from the ___E:Judaean Desert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaean_Desert)___ after rebuffing the temptation of ___E:Satan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satan)___ .

Jesus preaches around Galilee, and in ___E:Matthew 4:18–20 U:(https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Bible_(American_Standard)/Matthew#4:18)___ , ___E:his first disciples U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_disciples_of_Jesus)___ , who will eventually form the core of the early Church, encounter him and begin to travel with him.   This period includes the ___E:Sermon on the Mount U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sermon_on_the_Mount)___ , one of Jesus's major discourses,   as well as the ___E:calming of the storm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calming_of_the_storm)___ , the ___E:feeding of the 5,000 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feeding_of_the_5,000)___ , ___E:walking on water U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_walking_on_water)___ and other miracles and ___E:parables U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parables_of_Jesus)___ .
It ends with the ___E:Confession of Peter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confession_of_Peter)___ and the Transfiguration.

As Jesus travels towards Jerusalem, in the Perean ministry, he returns to the area where he was baptized, about a third of the way down from the ___E:Sea of Galilee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_of_Galilee)___ along the Jordan.

The ___E:final ministry in Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Jesus#Final_ministry_in_Jerusalem)___ begins with Jesus's ___E:triumphal entry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triumphal_entry_into_Jerusalem)___ into the city on ___E:Palm Sunday U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Sunday)___ .

In the Synoptic Gospels, during that week Jesus ___E:drives the money changers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleansing_of_the_Temple)___ from the ___E:Second Temple U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Temple)___ and ___E:Judas bargains to betray U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bargain_of_Judas)___ him. This period culminates in the ___E:Last Supper U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Supper)___ and the ___E:Farewell Discourse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell_Discourse)___ .
Near the beginning of his ministry, Jesus ___E:appoints twelve apostles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commissioning_of_the_Twelve_Apostles)___ .

In Matthew and Mark, despite Jesus only briefly requesting that they join him, Jesus's first four apostles, who were fishermen, are described as immediately consenting, and abandoning their nets and boats to do so.  In John, Jesus's first two apostles were disciples of John the Baptist.
The Baptist sees Jesus and calls him the Lamb of God; the two hear this and follow Jesus.

In addition to the Twelve Apostles, the opening of the passage of the ___E:Sermon on the Plain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sermon_on_the_Plain)___ identifies a much larger group of people as disciples.

Also, in ___E:Luke 10:1–16 U:(https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Bible_(American_Standard)/Luke#10:1)___ Jesus sends ___E:70 or 72 of his followers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventy_disciples)___ in pairs to prepare towns for his prospective visit.
They are instructed to accept hospitality, heal the sick, and spread the word that the ___E:Kingdom of God U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_God)___ is coming.

In the Synoptics, Jesus teaches extensively, often in ___E:parables U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parable)___ ,  about the Kingdom of God (or, in Matthew, the ___E:Kingdom of Heaven U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Heaven_(Gospel_of_Matthew))___ ).
The Kingdom is described as both imminent  and already present in the ministry of Jesus.
Jesus promises inclusion in the Kingdom for those who accept his message.

He talks of the " ___E:Son of Man U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_of_man_(Christianity))___ ", an ___E:apocalyptic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apocalypse)___ figure who will come to gather the chosen.

Jesus calls people to repent their sins and to devote themselves completely to God.  He tells his followers to adhere to ___E:Jewish law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_law)___ , although he is perceived by some to have broken the law himself, for example regarding the ___E:Sabbath U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabbath)___ .
When asked what the greatest commandment is, Jesus replies: "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind ...

And a second is like it: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself. ' "  Other ethical teachings of Jesus include ___E:loving your enemies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_5:44)___ , refraining from hatred and lust, ___E:turning the other cheek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turning_the_other_cheek)___ , and forgiving people who have sinned against you.
John's Gospel presents the teachings of Jesus not merely as his own preaching, but as divine ___E:revelation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revelation)___ .

John the Baptist, for example, states in ___E:John 3:34 U:(https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Bible_(American_Standard)/John#3:34)___ : "He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure." In ___E:John 7:16 U:(https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Bible_(American_Standard)/John#7:16)___ Jesus says, "My teaching is not mine but his who sent me." He asserts the same thing in ___E:John 14:10 U:(https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Bible_(American_Standard)/John#14:10)___ : "Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me?
The words that I say to you I do not speak on my own; but the Father who dwells in me does his works."
Approximately 30 parables form about one-third of Jesus's recorded teachings.
The parables appear within longer sermons and at other places in the narrative.
They often contain symbolism, and usually relate the physical world to the ___E:spiritual U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirituality)___ .
Common themes in these tales include the kindness and generosity of God and the perils of transgression.

Some of his parables, such as the ___E:Prodigal Son U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prodigal_Son)___ ,  are relatively simple, while others, such as the ___E:Growing Seed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parable_of_the_Growing_Seed)___ ,  are sophisticated, profound and abstruse.

When asked by his disciples why he speaks in parables to the people, Jesus replies that the chosen disciples have been given to "know the secrets of the kingdom of heaven", unlike the rest of their people, "For the one who has will be given more and he will have in abundance.
But the one who does not have will be deprived even more", going on to say that the majority of their generation have grown "dull hearts" and thus are unable to understand.
In the gospel accounts, Jesus devotes a large portion of his ministry to performing ___E:miracles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miracle)___ , especially healings.
The miracles can be classified into two main categories: healing miracles and nature miracles.

The healing miracles include cures for physical ailments, ___E:exorcisms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exorcism)___ ,   and ___E:resurrections of the dead U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miracles_of_Jesus#Resurrection_of_the_dead)___ .

The nature miracles show Jesus's power over nature, and include ___E:turning water into wine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turning_water_into_wine)___ , walking on water, and calming a storm, among others.
Jesus states that his miracles are from a divine source.

When his opponents accuse him of performing exorcisms by the power of ___E:Beelzebub U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beelzebub)___ , the prince of demons, Jesus counters that he performs them by the "Spirit of God" ( ___E:Matthew 12:28 U:(https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Bible_(American_Standard)/Matthew#12:28)___ ) or "finger of God", arguing that all logic suggests that Satan would not let his demons assist the Children of God because it would divide Satan's house and bring his kingdom to desolation; he also asks his opponents that if he exorcises by Beelzebub, "by whom do your sons cast them out?".

In ___E:Matthew 12:31–32 U:(https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Bible_(American_Standard)/Matthew#12:28)___ , he goes on to say that while all manner of sin, "even insults against God" or "insults against the son of man", shall be forgiven, whoever insults goodness (or "The ___E:Holy Spirit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Spirit)___ ") shall never be forgiven; they carry the guilt of their sin forever.
In John, Jesus's miracles are described as "signs", performed to prove his mission and divinity.

In the Synoptics, when asked by some teachers of the Law and some Pharisees to give miraculous signs to prove his authority, Jesus refuses,  saying that no sign shall come to corrupt and evil people except the sign of the prophet ___E:Jonah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonah)___ .

Also, in the Synoptic Gospels, the crowds regularly respond to Jesus's miracles with awe and press on him to heal their sick. In John's Gospel, Jesus is presented as unpressured by the crowds, who often respond to his miracles with trust and faith.
One characteristic shared among all miracles of Jesus in the gospel accounts is that he performed them freely and never requested or accepted any form of payment.
The gospel episodes that include descriptions of the miracles of Jesus also often include teachings, and the miracles themselves involve an element of teaching.
Many of the miracles teach the importance of faith.

In the ___E:cleansing of ten lepers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleansing_ten_lepers)___ and the ___E:raising of Jairus's daughter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raising_of_Jairus%27s_daughter)___ , for instance, the beneficiaries are told that their healing was due to their faith.
At about the middle of each of the three Synoptic Gospels are two significant events: the Confession of ___E:Peter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter)___ and the Transfiguration of Jesus.
These two events are not mentioned in the Gospel of John.
In his Confession, Peter tells Jesus, "You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God."    Jesus affirms that Peter's confession is divinely revealed truth.
After the confession, Jesus tells his disciples about his upcoming death and resurrection.

In the Transfiguration,     Jesus takes Peter and two other apostles up an unnamed mountain, where "he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became dazzling white".
A bright cloud appears around them, and a voice from the cloud says, "This is my Son, the Beloved; with him I am well pleased; listen to him."

The description of the last week of the life of Jesus (often called ___E:Passion Week U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passion_Week)___ ) occupies about one-third of the narrative in the canonical gospels.
It starts with Jesus's ___E:triumphal entry into Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triumphal_entry_into_Jerusalem)___ and ends with his Crucifixion.
In the Synoptics, the last week in Jerusalem is the conclusion of the journey through Perea and Judea that Jesus began in Galilee.

Jesus rides a young donkey into Jerusalem, reflecting the tale of ___E:the Messiah's Donkey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Messiah%27s_Donkey)___ , an oracle from the ___E:Book of Zechariah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Zechariah)___ in which the Jews' humble king enters Jerusalem this way.   People along the way lay cloaks and small branches of trees (known as ___E:palm fronds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_branch)___ ) in front of him and sing part of Psalms 118:25–26.
Jesus next expels the money changers from the Second Temple, accusing them of turning it into a den of thieves through their commercial activities.

He then prophesies about the coming destruction, including false prophets, wars, earthquakes, celestial disorders, persecution of the faithful, the appearance of an "abomination of desolation", and unendurable tribulations.
The "Son of Man", he says, will dispatch angels to gather the faithful from all parts of the earth.
Jesus warns that these events will occur in the lifetimes of the hearers.
In John, the Cleansing of the Temple occurs at the beginning of Jesus's ministry instead of at the end.

Jesus comes into conflict with the Jewish elders, such as when they ___E:question his authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Authority_of_Jesus_questioned)___ and when he ___E:criticizes them and calls them hypocrites U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woes_of_the_Pharisees)___ .   ___E:Judas Iscariot U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judas_Iscariot)___ , one of the ___E:twelve apostles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelve_apostles)___ , secretly strikes a bargain with the Jewish elders, agreeing to betray Jesus to them for ___E:30 silver coins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/30_silver_coins)___ .

The Gospel of John recounts two other feasts in which Jesus taught in Jerusalem before the Passion Week.   In ___E:Bethany U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethany)___ , a village near Jerusalem, Jesus ___E:raises Lazarus from the dead U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raising_of_Lazarus)___ .

This potent sign  increases the tension with authorities,  who conspire to kill him.   ___E:Mary of Bethany U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_of_Bethany)___ anoints Jesus's feet, foreshadowing his entombment.
Jesus then makes his messianic entry into Jerusalem.
The cheering crowds greeting Jesus as he enters Jerusalem add to the animosity between him and the establishment.
In John, Jesus has already cleansed the Second Temple during an earlier Passover visit to Jerusalem.
John next recounts Jesus's Last Supper with his disciples.
The Last Supper is the final meal that Jesus shared with his twelve apostles in Jerusalem before his crucifixion.

The Last Supper is mentioned in all four canonical gospels; Paul's ___E:First Epistle to the Corinthians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Epistle_to_the_Corinthians)___  also refers to it.    During the meal, ___E:Jesus predicts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_predicts_his_betrayal)___ that one of his apostles will betray him.  Despite each Apostle's assertion that he would not betray him, Jesus reiterates that the betrayer would be one of those present.
Matthew 26:23–25 and John 13:26–27 identify Judas as the traitor.

In the Synoptics, Jesus takes bread, breaks it, and gives it to the disciples, saying, "This is my body, which is given for you." He then has them all drink from a cup, saying, "This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood."    The Christian ___E:sacrament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacrament)___ or ___E:ordinance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordinance_(Christian))___ of the ___E:Eucharist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eucharist)___ is based on these events.

Although the Gospel of John does not include a description of the bread-and-wine ritual during the Last Supper, most scholars agree that John 6:22–59 (the ___E:Bread of Life Discourse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bread_of_Life_Discourse)___ ) has a eucharistic character and resonates with the ___E:institution narratives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origin_of_the_Eucharist#Institution_narratives)___ in the Synoptic Gospels and in the Pauline writings on the Last Supper.
In all four gospels, Jesus predicts that Peter will deny knowledge of him three times before the ___E:cock U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rooster)___ crows the next morning.
In Luke and John, the prediction is made during the Supper.

In Matthew and Mark, the prediction is made after the Supper; Jesus also predicts that all his disciples will desert him.   The Gospel of John provides the only account of ___E:Jesus washing his disciples' feet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maundy_(foot_washing))___ after the meal.  John also includes a long sermon by Jesus, preparing his disciples (now without Judas) for his departure.

Chapters 14–17 of the Gospel of John are known as the ___E:Farewell Discourse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell_Discourse)___ and are a significant source of ___E:Christological U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christological)___ content.
In the Synoptics, Jesus and his disciples go to the garden ___E:Gethsemane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gethsemane)___ , where Jesus prays to be spared his coming ordeal.
Then Judas comes with an armed mob, sent by the chief priests, ___E:scribes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scribe#Judaism)___ and elders.
He ___E:kisses Jesus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_of_Judas)___ to identify him to the crowd, which then ___E:arrests Jesus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrest_of_Jesus)___ .
In an attempt to stop them, an unnamed disciple of Jesus uses a sword to cut off the ear ___E:of a man U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malchus)___ in the crowd.
After Jesus's arrest, his disciples go into hiding, and Peter, when questioned, thrice ___E:denies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denial_of_Peter)___ knowing Jesus.
After the third denial, Peter hears the cock crow and recalls Jesus's prediction about his denial.
Peter then weeps bitterly.
In John 18:1–11, Jesus does not pray to be spared his crucifixion, as the gospel portrays him as scarcely touched by such human weakness.
The people who arrest him are ___E:Roman soldiers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Roman_army)___ and Temple guards.
Instead of being betrayed by a kiss, Jesus proclaims his identity, and when he does, the soldiers and officers fall to the ground.
The gospel identifies Peter as the disciple who used the sword, and Jesus rebukes him for it.

After his arrest, Jesus is taken late at night to the private residence of the high priest, ___E:Caiaphas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caiaphas)___ , who had been installed by Pilate's predecessor, the Roman procurator ___E:Valerius Gratus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valerius_Gratus)___ .

The ___E:Sanhedrin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanhedrin)___ was a Jewish judicial body.  The gospel accounts differ on the ___E:details of the trials U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanhedrin_trial_of_Jesus)___ .

In Matthew 26:57, Mark 14:53, and Luke 22:54, Jesus is taken to the house of the high priest, Caiaphas, where he is ___E:mocked U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mocking_of_Jesus)___ and beaten that night.
Early the next morning, the chief priests and scribes lead Jesus away into their council.
John 18:12–14 states that Jesus is first taken to ___E:Annas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annas)___ , Caiaphas's father-in-law, and then to the high priest.

During the trials Jesus speaks very little, mounts no defence, and gives very infrequent and indirect answers to the priests' questions, prompting an officer to slap him. In Matthew 26:62, Jesus's unresponsiveness leads Caiaphas to ask him, "Have you no answer?".
In Mark 14:61, the high priest then asks Jesus, "Are you the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed One?".

Jesus replies, " ___E:I am U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_am_(biblical_term))___ ", and then predicts the coming of the Son of Man.  This provokes Caiaphas to tear his own robe in anger and to accuse Jesus of blasphemy.
In Matthew and Luke, Jesus's answer is more ambiguous:   in Matthew 26:64, he responds, "You have said so", and in Luke 22:70 he says, "You say that I am."

The Jewish elders take Jesus to ___E:Pilate's Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pilate%27s_Court)___ and ask the Roman governor, ___E:Pontius Pilate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontius_Pilate)___ , to judge and condemn Jesus for various allegations: subverting the nation, opposing the payment of tribute, claiming to be Christ, a king, and claiming to be the son of God. [q]  The use of the word "king" is central to the discussion between Jesus and Pilate.

In John 18:36, Jesus states, "My kingdom is not from this world", but he does not unequivocally deny being the King of the Jews.   In Luke 23:7–15, Pilate realizes that Jesus is a Galilean, and thus comes under the jurisdiction of ___E:Herod Antipas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herod_Antipas)___ , the ___E:Tetrarch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herodian_Tetrarchy)___ of Galilee and Perea.
Pilate sends Jesus to Herod to be tried,  but Jesus says almost nothing in response to Herod's questions.

Herod and his soldiers mock Jesus, put an expensive robe on him to make him look like a king, and return him to Pilate,  who then calls together the Jewish elders and announces that he has "not found this man guilty".
Observing a Passover custom of the time, Pilate allows one prisoner chosen by the crowd to be released.

He gives the people a choice between Jesus and a murderer called ___E:Barabbas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barabbas)___ ( בר-אבא or Bar-abbâ , "son of the father", from the common given name Abba : 'father').
Persuaded by the elders,  the mob chooses to release Barabbas and crucify Jesus.

Pilate writes a sign in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek that reads "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews" (abbreviated as ___E:INRI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INRI)___ in depictions) to be affixed to Jesus's cross,   then ___E:scourges Jesus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellation_of_Christ)___ and sends him to be crucified.

The soldiers place a ___E:crown of thorns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_of_thorns)___ on Jesus's head and ridicule him as the King of the Jews. They beat and taunt him before taking him to ___E:Calvary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvary)___ ,  also called Golgotha, for crucifixion.
Jesus's crucifixion is described in all four canonical gospels.

After the trials, Jesus is led to Calvary ___E:carrying his cross U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christ_Carrying_the_Cross)___ ; the route traditionally thought to have been taken is known as the ___E:Via Dolorosa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Via_Dolorosa)___ .

The three Synoptic Gospels indicate that ___E:Simon of Cyrene U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_of_Cyrene)___ assists him, having been compelled by the Romans to do so.   In Luke 23:27–28, Jesus tells the women in the multitude of people following him not to weep for him but for themselves and their children.
At Calvary, Jesus is offered a sponge soaked in a concoction usually offered as a ___E:painkiller U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Painkiller)___ .
According to Matthew and Mark, he refuses it.
The soldiers then crucify Jesus and ___E:cast lots U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sortes_(ancient_Rome))___ for his clothes.

Above Jesus's head on the cross is Pilate's multilingual inscription, "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews." Soldiers and passersby ___E:mock U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mocking_of_Jesus)___ him about it. Two convicted thieves are crucified along with Jesus.
In Matthew and Mark, both thieves mock Jesus.

In Luke, ___E:one of them U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impenitent_thief)___ rebukes Jesus, while ___E:the other U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penitent_thief)___ defends him.    Jesus tells the latter: "today you will be with me in Paradise."
